title: Signal · Friday 13 November
overview: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia with immediate effect, the finance ministry fines former Credit Suisse chair Urs Rohner, and wealth platform FNZ pulls back to its core markets.

top.headline: Update: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief; CFO Colette Kress steps in
top.summary: Nvidia's board said on 12 November that Jensen Huang, co-founder and chief executive for 33 years, had resigned as president, CEO and director with immediate effect. Colette Kress, chief financial officer since 2013, becomes interim CEO while the board looks for a permanent successor.
top.background: Huang left after reports of an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy and another with one of his direct reports, according to TechCrunch. Nvidia, worth about USD 3.8 trillion, had no succession plan.
top.why: Nvidia designs the chips the AI boom runs on, so an interim leader and an open succession add uncertainty for the cloud providers and AI labs that banks buy from.
top.watch_next: Kress presents quarterly results on 17 November, and Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to Bloomberg and NBC News.

top.headline: Finance ministry fines former Credit Suisse chair Urs Rohner over surveillance affair
top.summary: The Federal Department of Finance has penalised Urs Rohner, Credit Suisse chair from 2011 to 2021, for knowingly giving FINMA false information about the bank's surveillance of staff, according to SRF Investigativ and Republik. The order of 20 October, not yet final, sets a fine of CHF 24,840 and 144 daily fines of CHF 690, suspended.
top.background: Rohner signed the bank's October 2019 answer to FINMA, which called the watching of Iqbal Khan an isolated incident; the ministry found seven operations planned or carried out from 2016 to 2019. It says he deliberately concealed one operation's link to then chief executive Tidjane Thiam.
top.why: A former chair is held personally to account for what he told FINMA, a reminder to boards that answers to the supervisor must be complete and impartial.
top.watch_next: Rohner rejects the allegations and has asked for a judicial review, so the case moves to the Federal Criminal Court in Bellinzona.

top.headline: Wealth platform FNZ cuts jobs and narrows its footprint to core markets
top.summary: FNZ, which administers USD 2.5 trillion for 30 million investors, said on 12 November it will cut headcount, reduce global and regional overheads and narrow its geographic footprint. Offices in Singapore, the Nordics, Spain, Italy and France are set to close, leaving the UK, Australia, New Zealand and the US as core markets, according to Scottish Financial News.
top.background: Stephen Welch became executive chair and interim chief executive two months ago, after Blythe Masters left. FNZ says years of growth left it with a complex structure, bespoke client delivery and higher costs.
top.why: Banks and wealth managers on FNZ in the markets it is leaving will want to know how support and the roadmap will be delivered, and stricter scoping and pricing of client work may raise their project costs.
top.watch_next: How FNZ serves existing clients in the markets it leaves, and whether it names a permanent chief executive.

items.headline: Lucerne wealthtech Allocare joins Constellation Software's Volaris Group
items.summary: Allocare, which makes portfolio management, compliance and reporting software for banks, independent wealth managers and family offices, has belonged to Volaris since 1 October, it said on 12 November. It keeps its brand and operational independence; no price was disclosed. Chief executive David Popp said the owner will help it develop faster in the age of AI (translated from German).
items.why: Volaris buys to hold, which favours product continuity for Allocare's Swiss clients; pricing and the AI roadmap are the things to watch.

items.headline: Rothschild & Co hires Lombard Odier's technology and operations head as group CTOO
items.summary: Rothschild & Co has named Geoffroy de Ridder group chief technology and operations officer, a new role he takes up in December alongside the same post for wealth and asset management, finews reports. He led technology and operations at Lombard Odier and earlier held senior roles at UBS, including wealth management COO for Asia Pacific.
items.why: Rothschild puts technology and operations under one group executive as it pushes digital change, and Lombard Odier must now fill that seat in Geneva.

items.headline: Avaloq: 44 percent of UK investors want AI out of product recommendations
items.summary: UK wealth managers handle larger client books and spend more time on administration than peers elsewhere, according to Avaloq research reported by WealthBriefing on 12 November. Ninety percent of UK managers expect AI to benefit the industry, while 44 percent of UK investors want it removed from product recommendations.
items.why: Firms putting AI into advice will need to show clients where it sits and who checks it, because adviser enthusiasm is running ahead of client trust.

items.headline: HSBC UK adds Stripe-powered Tap to Pay to its business banking app
items.summary: Sole traders and small businesses banking with HSBC UK can now accept contactless payments on a compatible smartphone, without a separate card reader, by switching the feature on in the bank's business app, Fintech News Switzerland reports. Stripe powers the service.
items.why: Banks are folding card acceptance into their own apps through payment partners, which puts pressure on standalone card-reader providers serving small merchants.

items.headline: Swiss banks generated CHF 74.5 billion in value added in 2025, SBA study finds
items.summary: Banks' direct gross value added reached CHF 43.8 billion in 2025, about 5.1 percent of the Swiss total, with 157,700 full-time staff, according to a BAK Economics study for the Swiss Bankers Association reported by Keystone-SDA. With indirect effects the total was CHF 74.5 billion and about 338,700 jobs; banking service exports were CHF 24.4 billion.
items.why: The figures arrive ten days before the National Council committee debates the UBS capital bill, and give the industry fresh numbers for that argument.

items.headline: Zurich lifts property and casualty premiums 7 percent despite European storm losses
items.summary: Gross written premiums in property and casualty rose 7 percent on a comparable basis to USD 42.1 billion in the first nine months, with motor up 14 percent, Zurich said on 12 November. Storms in Switzerland, Germany and Italy raised the catastrophe claims ratio to 3.2 percent from 1.4 percent; the estimated Swiss Solvency Test ratio reached 271 percent.
items.why: Rising weather losses even in strong years keep catastrophe modelling and claims automation near the top of insurers' technology budgets.

items.headline: Franc rally squeezes carry trades as the SMI sets a record above 15,200
items.summary: Year-to-date returns from selling the franc against the euro fell to 0.1 percent last week from 3.4 percent at the end of September, Bloomberg reports, after the franc touched 0.91376 per euro, its strongest since May. SNB officials told the government on 11 November the bank is ready to act in currency markets if needed. The SMI reached a record 15,200.17 points on 12 November.
items.why: A stronger franc shrinks foreign-currency fees once converted into francs, which keeps Swiss banks' cost programmes under pressure into 2027.

items.headline: Metro Bank launches a formal sale process as part of a strategic review
items.summary: Metro Bank said on 12 November its board is reviewing options, including a formal sale, and that it is in no active discussions with any potential bidder. The UK lender, valued at GBP 1.2 billion before the news according to Reuters, reaffirmed targets of more than 13 percent return on tangible equity in the fourth quarter and more than 18 percent in 2028.
items.why: A sale would extend consolidation among UK mid-sized lenders, where deposit costs and technology budgets decide who stays independent.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model for everyday coding and agents
items.summary: Google said on 12 November that Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default setting, ahead of Gemini 4 Argon's 50, and costs USD 1.50 per million input tokens and USD 7.50 per million output tokens across a 1 million token window. It is coming to the Gemini app, Search, the API and Gemini for business.
items.why: A cheaper execution model that pairs with frontier models improves the cost case for high-volume bank work such as document handling and code changes.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Architecture & TOM can propose a design that switches between a frontier model and a fast one; Google's Orchestrator did this with 24 percent less quota on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot for hours worldwide
items.summary: Microsoft said on 12 November that a large number of servers had become unexpectedly unavailable, cutting access to Exchange Online mailboxes in any region, with Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR also hit, TechCrunch reports. Restarted servers kept failing once traffic returned, and early on 13 November Microsoft was still bringing infrastructure back in stages, according to SRF.
items.why: For banks running mail, meetings and security monitoring on Microsoft 365, it is a live test of the concentration risk DORA and FINMA's outsourcing rules ask them to plan for.

items.headline: Breach at AI host Fireworks exposes Notion AI chat transcripts
items.summary: Fireworks AI, which serves open models to developers, said attackers breached its cloud provider and reached a development system holding customers' billing information and some datasets, TechCrunch reports. Notion said about 1 percent of its customers were affected, including chat transcripts from its AI Insights feature. It is the second incident at Fireworks in two months.
items.why: Prompts and outputs are client data, so banks' vendor reviews should reach the inference host behind each AI tool as well as the tool itself.

items.headline: United Airlines blocks personal AI agents from booking, citing credential risks
items.summary: United said on 12 November it will restrict unauthorised third-party AI agents from its booking and account systems, directly and through agencies and aggregators, warning that shared credentials can lead to unintended purchases or account changes. TechCrunch notes that Bank of America recently urged customers not to share passwords with AI assistants.
items.why: Banks face the same choice: block customers' agents, or offer them a sanctioned, scoped way in before sharing passwords with assistants becomes routine.

items.headline: T-Systems Switzerland launches a sovereign AI platform for firms with sensitive data
items.summary: The Swiss AI Factory combines GPU capacity in T-Systems' Swiss data centres, open-source models and an AI gateway that applies anonymisation, access control and audit logs, Netzwoche reports. Customers choose their models and where data is processed and stored, and can reach more than 10,000 GPUs in Germany for training and heavy workloads.
items.why: It gives Swiss banks another locally hosted option to compare with hyperscaler regions when client data has to stay in Switzerland.

Swiss consultancies use AI widely; 55 percent see no effect on prices or margins
EPFL will launch a bachelor's degree in artificial intelligence in autumn 2027
Michael Page: Swiss pay broadly flat for 2027, while AI specialists see sharp rises

say_it_today: Swiss consultancies say AI is now part of daily work, yet 55 percent see no effect on price, project length or margin. With clients already expecting faster delivery, the open question is who keeps the productivity gain.
